statement: One node process owns exactly ONE ControlPlaneReadinessService (and therefore one ReadinessPlanningSnapshotOwner), composed by the existing node-level composition owner (the bootstrap control-plane setup, which already constructs it and hands it to the node-scoped RebalanceCoordinator container) with an explicit lifecycle — create, subscribe, use, shutdown, reconstruct — and every partition rebalancer and planning/readiness consumer in the process consumes that same instance through explicit injection from the container; no partition, rebalancer, or dispatch service constructs its own readiness service when the container is present, and no module-global singleton is introduced. Invariants: (O1) in a process hosting many partitions, ControlPlaneReadinessService constructions == 1 on the real composition path (bootstrap setup -> coordinator -> partition rebalancer) — restoring per-rebalancer construction must red; (O2) r1.controlPlaneReadinessService === r2.controlPlaneReadinessService === r3.controlPlaneReadinessService === coordinator.controlPlaneReadinessService through that real path, not a test-only stub; (O3) semantics unchanged — for the same authoritative state the shared instance yields the same readiness/planning decisions as an identically configured standalone instance across seed, joiner, transitional membership, live veto, planning refresh and completed-snapshot reuse; (O4) one cache/source change causes exactly one readiness-owner cache-change invocation in the process, measured through the real subscription path, not one per hosted partition; (O5) shutting down and reconstructing the node owner unsubscribes the old service (no listener left on the cache, planning queue stopped) and constructs the new one exactly once with no duplicate listeners; (O6) creating, shutting down, or rebalancing a partition never creates, resets, or destroys the node-level readiness service; (ENGAGEMENT) under the formation-shaped fixture the seed process holds one planning owner, zero rebuilds by unused owners, and one cache-change fan-out per source change, with a red-on-revert proof; (BOUNDED-WORK) readiness planning work scales with authoritative changes, not with the number of hosted partitions — planning rebuilds are independent of N partition rebalancers. Explicit non-scope, byte-for-byte unless required for injection plumbing: the six-table floored generation, the 250ms latch, planning token semantics, the completed-snapshot reuse predicate, buildOptions variants, mixed-clock handling, the critical topology settling gate, routing readiness, node_ready_lease_incomplete consumption, storage_reservation_reconcile, and the frozen critical-placement candidate.
